ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and RMI domestic proscribed persons list; mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons and their close associates; continuous monitoring for adverse media, negative legal events, and jurisdiction-specific high-risk flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Business Registrar Online Filing Portal (Office of the Registrar of Business Entities, Ministry of Finance and Banking)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; non-English names may be accepted only in Latin transliteration. A corporate suffix must be present, such as 'Business Corporation', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an accepted abbreviation. Ambiguous transliterations or homophones similar to existing registered names are subject to rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its registered agent may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal shall state the legal grounds for contesting the refusal, append the original rejection notice, and propose a corrected name if applicable. A negative appeal decision may be further submitted to the Minister of Finance for discretionary reconsideration. Unused name reservations lapse after 30 days; the applicant may submit a fresh name reservation after the lapse.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible through a licensed registered agent in Majuro. No physical trading office or employees are required in the Marshall Islands for a non-resident Business Corporation engaged in wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules. The statutory registered office may be the agent's address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated unannounced physical inspection probability of 1–3% annually for a non-resident trading entity with no physical premises; inspections overwhelmingly occur only on anti-money-laundering suspicion or regulatory complaint.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Title 23 of the RMI Revised Code), Articles 1 to 4 (Formation, Registered Office and Agent, Shares, Directors and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Republic of the Marshall Islands (acting through a licensed registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-I) submitted to the Registrar of Corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by RMI statute. The authorized capital may be expressed in U.S. dollars or another permitted currency; the corporation must authorize at least one share of no-par or par-value stock. Shares may be issued for cash, property, or services, and the board may rely on a capital subscription agreement where banking onboarding requires evidence of initial funding.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of this Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands is approved and the registered agent is directed to file the Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations. RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent named in the Articles are adopted. RESOLVED, that the initial subscriber subscribes for the number of authorized shares stated in the Articles and the board fixes the initial director slate. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as officers: President, Secretary and Treasurer. RESOLVED, that the President and Treasurer are authorized to execute banking documentation, maintain corporate records, and engage the registered agent for statutory compliance. RESOLVED, that all prior actions taken in connection with formation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent duly licensed under the Business Corporations Act; name reservation through the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain an RMI-licensed registered agent, submit a proposed corporate name for preliminary clearance, and reserve the exact name using the official reservation form. The reservation is valid for a statutory period and must be issued in the name of the intended corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or unavailability, file a new reservation with an alternate name within 5 business days; any correction request is processed through the same registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and notary public; RMI registered agent reviews for statutory compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation setting forth the corporate name, registered agent and office in the Marshall Islands, authorized capital structure, share classes and voting rights, the initial board of directors, and any permitted limitation of liability under the Act. The incorporator executes the Articles; signatures must be notarized and dated. The registered agent coordinates any legalization or apostille if the original execution is done outside the Marshall Islands.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered agent to act
Address of registered office in Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or queries the filing, correct the identified provisions and resubmit the revised Articles through the registered agent within 7 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation with Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation, registered agent consent, and the applicable filing fee to the Registrar. The filing may be performed electronically through the registered agent. Upon acceptance, the Registrar endorses the Articles with the date of filing, assigns a corporate registration number, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Copy of the incorporator's notarized identity document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for missing fee or invalid notarization, pay the additional fee or resubmit the notarized signature within 14 business days; the Registrar will proceed without reopening the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Bylaws and Appoint Initial Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, sole initial director, and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator or initial director adopts the corporate bylaws, sets the record date and fiscal year, and executes written resolutions appointing the initial directors and officers. The board resolutions must be maintained in the corporate minute book and made available for inspection by the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent identifies a governance deficiency, amend the bylaws and re-execute the resolutions before bank onboarding or other regulated actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Filings and Corporate Record Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RMI registered agent; Registrar of Corporations; Ministry of Finance as applicable for annual franchise tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the required post-incorporation acknowledgments, maintain the registered agent designation, pay any applicable annual franchise tax if a resident or doing-business entity status applies, and ensure the registered office remains current. Update the corporate register of shareholders and directors whenever changes occur.
required_dossiers: Annual compliance schedule from registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual compliance is missed, file a late corrected return with the registered agent and pay the applicable restoration fee within 30 days to avoid administrative dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Banking Facilities and Issue Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank; RMI corporate administrator; Compliance officer of the appointed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue the share certificates to the subscribing shareholder against a board resolution covering the share subscription. Present a completed corporate onboarding package to the chosen bank, including the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, first board resolution, officer identification, and a beneficial ownership declaration compatible with the bank's enhanced due diligence for petrochemical trading and letter-of-credit payment rails.
required_dossiers: First board resolution for share issuance and bank authority
Passport copies of directors and ultimate beneficial owner
Business plan or invoice forecast for the bulk petrochemical polymer trading activity
AML/KYC forms of the target bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a clarification notice for a higher AML medium-risk rating, provide supplemental trade documentation, commercial contracts, and the source-of-funds declaration within 20 business days; appeal declined accounts through the bank's compliance escalation procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None — this non-resident Business Corporation conducts wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules with no physical presence, manufacturing, warehousing, or importation into the Marshall Islands; no local industrial license is triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — activity is governed solely by the Business Corporations Act and any banking or trade finance documentation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 5: administrative and trading-only activity with no land disturbance, storage, discharge, or emission in the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the corporation has no local physical operations; zero point-source wastewater discharge, zero fugitive VOC emissions, and no bulk polymer storage within RMI territory. If the company later establishes a local office or bonded warehouse, an EIA registration will be required for any solvent use, stormwater runoff, or solid waste generation, in accordance with Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no local premises, fire load, or structural occupancy exists to be inspected by the RMI Fire Safety Division. The corporation must only maintain safe home-office practices where no RMI workplace certificate is required. Should a later RMI office lease be entered into, the local landlord's building permit and fire safety clearance must be verified before staff occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) levies no income tax and therefore maintains no dedicated national income tax authority and no income tax e-filing portal. The relevant administrative bodies are: (1) Ministry of Finance & Treasury, Revenue and Customs Division (Majuro), which administers customs duties, excise duties and the Business License Fee; official site: www.finance.gov.mh; (2) Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Majuro), which administers incorporation, annual reports and the annual corporate franchise fee under the Business Corporations Act (BCA); filings are made through ARARM-licensed registered agents; and (3) Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA), which administers payroll contributions for local employees. No TIN-issuing income tax office exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: There is no income-tax TIN. Steps to obtain the statutory identifiers for a foreign-owned Non-Resident Business Corporation: (1) engage an ARARM-licensed registered agent in Majuro, as the BCA requires a resident agent; (2) file Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations; (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the corporate registration number, which is the entity's primary statutory identifier; (4) if the entity will conduct any business activity with nexus inside the RMI, apply to the Business License Office for an annual Business License and obtain the license number; the annual fee is 3% of gross revenue subject to statutory minimums and sector-specific flat fees; a purely non-resident offshore trader with no RMI-source sales, no office and no local employees does not require a license; (5) if the entity employs RMI-based staff, register with MISSA and obtain an employer account number; (6) if the entity imports goods into the RMI, register with Customs for an importer identification number. Non-resident BCs are not issued an income-tax TIN because no such tax exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone / Territorial_Scope: A Non-Resident Business Corporation is entirely outside the RMI tax net. The RMI has no corporate income tax, no personal income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties or fees, and no estate, gift, stamp or property tax on share capital. The only state impost on a BCA entity is a fixed annual corporate franchise/annual report fee, which is not profit-based. A BC deriving trading income from wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules (ISIC 4669) to non-RMI buyers is tax-exempt in the RMI regardless of where contracts are executed, provided no local business license nexus is created.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable: the RMI has no income tax statute, so there are no check-the-box classifications, no hybrid-mismatch elections and no pass-through tax elections. Corporate-form elections available under the BCA include conversion or continuation into an RMI Limited Liability Company or Limited Partnership, which may be relevant to beneficial owners' home-jurisdiction planning; designation of the registered agent; and, in the shipping context, election to register vessels under the RMI open registry, subjecting shipping income to annual tonnage fees rather than any revenue-based impost. An RMI entity is not eligible to make a U.S. check-the-box election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.business_license_levy_note: Under the Business License Act, any person 'carrying on business' in the RMI must obtain a Business License and pay an annual fee equal to 3% of gross revenue, subject to statutory minimums and sector-specific flat fees. A purely offshore polymer trading BC with no RMI-source sales, no RMI office and no RMI employees has no RMI business license nexus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.payroll_and_ssc_note: If the Non-Resident BC employs staff located in the Marshall Islands, it must register with MISSA; employer and employee social security contributions apply on covered wages up to the statutory wage base. No income or payroll tax is withheld because the RMI imposes no income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST or general sales tax exists in the Marshall Islands. The only indirect imposts are: (i) import customs duties under the RMI Customs Act and Tariff Act; (ii) excise duties on selective goods such as alcohol, tobacco, fuel and motor vehicles; and (iii) the Business License Fee of 3% of gross revenue, which is a revenue-based levy rather than a value-added or sales tax. There is consequently no indirect-tax registration regime for exporters.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST threshold exists. For customs purposes, there is no registration threshold; any importer must file a customs entry for goods entering the RMI. For Business License purposes, the obligation arises when business is carried on inside the RMI; the fee is 3% of gross revenue with statutory minimums. All amounts are in U.S. dollars, which is the official legal tender. Non-resident offshore trading does not meet the nexus test.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. There is no mandatory e-invoicing, no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based stamping regime and no digital tax-stamp requirement in the RMI. Customs declarations are lodged on prescribed paper or standard electronic forms with the Revenue and Customs Division at the port of entry; commercial invoices and bills of lading are retained as ordinary transaction records. No tax clearance certificate is required for export of goods in a non-RMI supply chain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.import_duty_context: If the BC ever imported PE or PP granules into the Marshall Islands, customs duty would be assessed ad valorem under the RMI Tariff Act on the c.i.f. value; however, the target offshore wholesale trading model does not trigger import duty.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — the RMI levies no VAT or GST, so there is no export zero-rating provision, no export VAT refund mechanism and no zero-rated supplier status. A Non-Resident BC selling petrochemical polymers to overseas buyers is simply outside the RMI tax base. For RMI-flagged shipping operations, the equivalent feature is the tonnage-fee regime under the RMI Maritime Act: shipping income is not taxed by reference to profits or freight, and no refund mechanism exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Ocean Bill of Lading (negotiable or telex-released) evidencing movement of PE/PP granules from load port to discharge port
Commercial invoice and HS Chapter 39 packing list (HS 3901.10/3902.10) matching the terms of the Irrevocable Letter of Credit
Irrevocable Letter of Credit and SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment advices evidencing inward remittance of the purchase price
Export customs declaration issued by the exporting jurisdiction of the load port, not by the RMI, which issues no export declaration for this structure
Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and registered agent certificate of the RMI Business Corporation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.fx_controls_note: 0 indicates that no statutory deadline exists. The RMI uses the U.S. dollar as its sole legal tender and imposes no exchange controls, no foreign-exchange approval requirements and no repatriation deadline. The 180-day benchmark sometimes used in group policies is a commercial or foreign-country export-verification convention and has no force in the Marshall Islands.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT/GST refund system and therefore no indirect-tax clawback or fraudulent export zero-rating penalty regime in the RMI. The compliance risks for this structure are: (1) false filings with the Registrar of Corporations, which attract penalties and possible de-registration under the BCA; (2) failure to hold a Business License if the RMI authorities establish any local nexus, which could result in back assessment of the 3% gross-revenue fee, penalties, interest and license revocation; (3) customs offences such as under-declaration or smuggling if goods enter the RMI without duty payment, which attract forfeiture and penalties under the Customs legislation; and (4) substance-over-form recharacterization by beneficial owners' home jurisdictions if the offshore BC lacks economic substance. No RMI clawback of export refunds can arise because no such refunds are granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) maintains no indigenous central bank or monetary authority; the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender, and the U.S. Federal Reserve System acts as the de facto monetary anchor. Financial-sector supervision is exercised by the Marshall Islands Banking Commission under the Ministry of Finance, acting pursuant to the Banking Act 2010, the Business Corporations Act 1998, and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI has no separate national currency and no exchange-control legislation; capital and current account convertibility are therefore unrestricted. The USD is freely usable for all domestic and cross-border transactions, with no restrictions on profit repatriation, dividend distribution, liquidation proceeds, loan servicing, or disposal of capital. The only practical constraint on convertibility is the operational availability of U.S. dollar clearing through RMI-licensed banks' correspondent relationships and the compliance screening applied by international correspondent banks, not any statutory or regulatory impediment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, retention, or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts under RMI law. An exporting entity may freely retain and disburse all USD export proceeds without central-bank approval, conversion obligations, or time-limited surrender. The sole compliance requirement is AML/CFT record-keeping and transaction monitoring under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2018, including customer due diligence, threshold-based reporting, and accurate identification of the underlying trade in payment instructions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD Settlement Account
Operational USD Account and Trade Finance Clearing Account
Escrow and Development-Finance Account Only; not suited for commodity trade clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. RMI has not enacted a fintech or electronic-money institution licensing regime; the Banking Act 2010 reserves deposit-taking to licensed banks, and money services businesses require AML registration. Offshore digital EMIs licensed in third jurisdictions (e.g., HK MSO, FCA UK, MAS Singapore) may be used operationally as receivable or payable consolidation rails, provided the destination or source jurisdiction is not OFAC-sanctioned, but they are not recognized as banking counterparties by RMI regulators or by RMI banks, and major US correspondents will typically treat such entities as unlicensed high-risk intermediaries requiring explicit substance and license disclosure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the directors, the corporate secretary, and any authorized signatory of a non-resident Business Corporation. RMI-licensed banks require an in-person interview at the branch in Majuro or at a recognized RMI consular or representative office, together with presentation of original or notarized passport copies, proof of residential address, certified constitutional documents, certificate of good standing, board resolutions, and evidence of the group's organizational and funding structure. Remote account opening is not offered to offshore non-resident entities that lack an existing, verified relationship with the bank, and enhanced due diligence, including a professional reference from the introducing counsel or a licensed correspondent bank, is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore tax-exempt Business Corporation with no local staff, no physical office, and registration solely at a registered-agent address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantiation of economic substance and commercial reality: (1) current Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Registrar of Corporations; (2) certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; (3) full share register and registers of directors and beneficial owners; (4) board resolution appointing directors and officers and authorizing the opening of accounts and execution of treasury transactions; (5) fully executed master trading and supply agreements for virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules (ISIC 4669 / NAICS 424690), with recent commercial invoices and bank settlement references evidencing genuine cross-border trade; (6) interim management accounts or audited financial statements, as available, covering at least the most recent period; (7) corporate business plan demonstrating operating capability and anticipated transaction volume; and (8) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for each director and ultimate beneficial owner, supported by bank statements and tax or employment documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Petrochemical commodity trading subjected to enhanced scrutiny due to sanctions, diversion risk, and dual-use or embargo concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade-integrity and sanctions-compliance package: (1) executed end-user certificate and no-diversion declaration from each downstream buyer; (2) sanctions screening reports against UN Security Council consolidated lists, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU, UK OFSI, and FATF for all counterparties, intermediaries, vessels, shipping agents, and ports of loading and discharge; (3) complete trade cycle documentation set comprising proforma invoice, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and draft or issued documentary credit; (4) marine cargo insurance certificate and independent survey or inspection report; (5) a written legal opinion from specializing international trade counsel confirming the commodities fall outside controlled or sanctioned categories; and (6) evidence of the underlying financing and payment flow, linking the LC or wire transfer to the specific cargo movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Banking in a jurisdiction with no central bank and a perceived absence of sovereign financial-sector oversight or prudential regulation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory-and-sovereign-reassurance package: (1) the RMI Banking Commission license and a current regulatory status letter for the specific RMI bank selected as account provider; (2) a formal statement of the bank's compliance officer confirming the client profile fits the bank's product suite and risk appetite, to be obtained after onboarding; (3) confirmation that the USD is the statutory legal tender of the RMI under the Constitution, explaining why no foreign-exchange permit or central-bank approval is applicable; (4) documentary evidence of the provenance, amount, and purpose of the inbound capital injection, including the board resolution, subscription or intercompany loan agreement, and the remitter's bank statement; (5) relevant pages of the Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering progress or mutual-evaluation report summarizing RMI AML/CFT effectiveness; and (6) a certification of the entity's RMI tax-exempt or non-resident status, which is not itself a negative factor, accompanied by evidence that the entity is compliant with all annual RMI company-registry filings and good-standing requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from shareholders, group treasury, or intercompany lenders must be remitted in USD via SWIFT MT103 from the remitter's bank, clearing through Fedwire or CHIPS into the RMI bank's U.S. dollar correspondent account and ultimately credited to the entity's operational or escrow account. The payment instruction must carry the appropriate ISO 20022 compliance purpose code, preferably "CEQU" (capital and equity securities) or "GDCA" (capital operations), in the structured remittance block, supplemented by a free-text reference to the board resolution and subscription or loan agreement. Verification protocol: (a) full sanctions screening of the remitter, the remitter's bank, and any intermediary; (b) collection of source-of-funds evidence including the remitter's bank statement, board resolution, capital call, and subscription or shareholder loan agreement; and (c) posting to the equity or intercompany loan ledger only upon receipt of matching and consistency checks, with a required source-of-funds statement for every beneficial owner where total injected capital exceeds USD 100,000 or where the bank's screening threshold is lower.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for bulk polyethylene and polypropylene purchases shall be executed primarily through (a) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by SWIFT MT700, amended by SWIFT MT707, with the beneficiary receiving payment via MT103 or MT202 cover, or (b) direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for open-account settlements. USD transactions clear through correspondent accounts at major U.S. clearing banks (e.g., JPMorgan Chase, BNY Mellon, Citibank, or Bank of America N.A.) held by the RMI account provider, respecting OFAC and other embargo controls. Non-USD supplier payments (EUR, GBP, JPY, or CNY) must use the relevant clearing rails — TARGET2, CHAPS, BOJ-NET, or CIPS/CHATS respectively — with correct ISO 20022 purpose codes such as "GDDS" (goods traded) and matching invoice, packing list, bill of lading, insurance certificate, and LC terms. All outbound payments require a dual-signatory approval chain, pre-screening of the payee and its bank, and preservation of the full documentary evidence package for a minimum of five years under RMI record-keeping rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EUR, USD/JPY, USD/GBP and USD/CHF foreign exchange forwards and FX swaps, transacted with internationally regulated counterparties, for the hedging of non-USD trade payables and receivables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in CNY/USD, INR/USD, KRW/USD, and other restricted-currency pairs where the underlying trade is USD-denominated or the counterparty currency is non-convertible, to hedge against emerging-market exchange-rate volatility

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for longer-dated USD purchase obligations matched against EUR, JPY, or CNY revenue streams, where each leg is independently cash-settled and no illegal cross-border capital control is triggered

Plain-vanilla OTC foreign exchange options (call and put) as contained-risk, premium-limited hedges, permitted only where the counterparty is a licensed financial institution outside RMI and the option premium is documented in the entity's treasury policy

Synthetic commodity-linked or exotic derivatives are not permissible for a non-resident RMI Business Corporation without a recognized banking license or express regulatory authorization, and must not be entered into without separate board-approved treasury mandate and external legal advice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Annual Report (Section 107, Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (lodged through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the month of the incorporation anniversary; due on or before the last calendar day of the anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of US$400 imposed after the close of the anniversary month; continuing failure to file and pay for one reporting cycle may trigger administrative dissolution (strike-off) by the Registrar of Corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership / Controller Confirmation Certificate (Commercial Registered Agents Regulations 2019 AML/CFT record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (records available on demand to the Registrar of Corporations and the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the incorporation anniversary, certified by a director or officer; updated within 30 days of any share transfer or allotment affecting the register of members.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Uncorrected UBO data may cause registered agent resignation, a regulatory breach of the agent's license, and administrative strike-off of the corporation for failure to maintain statutory capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FATCA / CRS Entity Classification Self-Certification (Active NFFE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Competent Authority (Ministry of Finance / Treasury) transmitted through the licensed registered agent under the RMI-U.S. FATCA IGA and OECD CRS framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually synchronized with the reporting cycle of the registered agent; refreshed upon any material change in ownership or any U.S. tax indicia.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Stale or missing Active NFFE certification is reported to the RMI Competent Authority as a CRS/FATCA due-diligence failure, which may result in cross-border penalties and withdrawal of correspondent banking facilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No RMI statutory audit threshold applies to a non-resident tax-exempt Business Corporation; independent audit becomes mandatory only when required by a shareholders' agreement, a loan or LC facility, a foreign parent's consolidation rules, or the bank AML/KYC policy of the payment rails used (Swift_LC / Irrevocable_LC).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS preferred and accepted; US GAAP equally acceptable; the RMI does not promulgate a local GAAP; accounting records may be maintained at any location (typically Singapore, Dubai, or the trading office) provided they are retrievable by the registered agent and Registrar on request.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An annual confirmation certificate restating the registered members, directors, officers and every beneficial owner (25% threshold) must be executed by the BC and delivered to the licensed registered agent on or before each anniversary; share transfers and new allotments must be reflected simultaneously in the Register of Members and in an updated UBO schedule delivered to the agent within 30 days; failure to do so constitutes non-compliance with anti-money-laundering conditions attached to the agent's license and can result in agent resignation and administrative strike-off.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$700 - US$1,500 per year for licensed RMI registered agent, registered office, annual report preparation, and UBO/AML record maintenance; premium providers may charge US$1,800 - US$2,500 for complex groups.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit cost for a non-resident tax-exempt BC; voluntary certified audit engaged by lenders or shareholders typically ranges from US$3,000 to US$8,000 per annum for this wholesale trading profile.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0.0% for a Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporation deriving no income from sources within the Marshall Islands; a 3.0% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) is statutorily imposed on gross revenue derived from RMI-source business, which a properly structured non-resident BC must not earn.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, estate tax, and gift tax under Business Corporations Act (BCA) Section 107; the only recurring government impost is the annual franchise/administration fee (approximately US$200-US$500 depending on the authorized-capital bracket); no tax treaties or tax-sparing incentives are needed because the effective rate is zero on foreign-source wholesale trading income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Statement of Acknowledgment / Annual Franchise Tax Return (BCA Section 92) — filed electronically through the RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations e-filing portal (RMICorporation.org); no corporate income tax return is required for an exempt non-resident domestic corporation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before November 30 of each calendar year; a 60-day grace period is recognized in practice before the Registrar commences administrative dissolution proceedings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the corporation and its certificate-of-incorporation number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name exactly as registered; a non-resident BC must not indicate any RMI business address as its head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and registered-office street address in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain a licensed RMI registered agent; the registered office must be a physical address, not a P.O. box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal office and place of business address (outside the RMI for non-resident BCs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the operational trading address (e.g., Singapore, Dubai, or Rotterdam); confirm that no cargo storage, brokerage, or contracting activity is performed in the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals may serve; nominee directors must disclose their nominee status and the ultimate beneficial owner to the registered agent separately under the Beneficial Ownership Regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital, par value, and number of shares issued.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Minimum capital is not required; the annual franchise fee scales with the authorized-capital bracket, so keeping authorized capital at the US$50,000 standard bracket is typical.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of Acknowledgment — signed attestation that the corporation is not carrying on business in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A correct attestation is essential: earning RMI-source gross revenue would transform the entity into a GRT taxpayer and contradict the non-resident BC charter.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty typically equal to 10% of the annual franchise fee; failure to file within 60 days after the statutory deadline permits the Registrar to dissolve the corporation administratively. Reinstatement after dissolution requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and reinstatement fees, and contracts executed during the dissolved window are vulnerable to creditor challenge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gross Revenue Tax Return (GRT-1) — applicable only if the entity derives gross revenue from sources within the Marshall Islands; administered by the RMI Revenue Division and filed electronically or in paper form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly for RMI-source gross revenue with an annual reconciliation; nil filing is required where the entity holds a GRT registration but reports no RMI-source revenue.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly returns are due on the 30th day after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual reconciliation is due by the last day of the fourth month after the fiscal year-end (illustratively, 30 April for a 31 December year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax identification number, and address of the GRT-registered entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC without RMI-source revenue should generally not register; registration itself triggers quarterly filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue received during the period, segregated between RMI-source and foreign-source amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For bulk PE/PP granule trades, revenue is sourced where title passes and the services are rendered; offshore sales negotiated outside the RMI and settled by Swift LC in USD are foreign-source and excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: No deductions are allowed because the GRT is a gross-receipts tax; certain credits may be specified by Revenue Division rulings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim no cost-of-goods deduction for polymer purchases; the base is gross invoice value, not net trading margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of GRT at 3.0% on RMI-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If RMI-source revenue is nil, enter zero and submit a nil return by the deadline to avoid penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid GRT bears interest at the prescribed statutory rate; a penalty of up to 50% of the assessed tax may be imposed for gross negligence or intentional evasion; criminal liability includes a fine of up to US$1,000 and imprisonment of up to 3 years for willful false filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0.00% — the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions declared by a Business Corporation, regardless of the shareholder's residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable — the RMI maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreements and issues no tax residence certificates for non-resident domestic corporations. A repatriating shareholder should instead obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of Corporations and rely on statutory zero withholding; where the shareholder's home jurisdiction requires treaty protection, the analysis must be performed under that jurisdiction's domestic law because no RMI DTA relief is available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0.00% statutory withholding on interest and royalty payments made by an RMI Business Corporation to non-residents; no treaty-reduced rates are required because the domestic rate is already zero.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None prescribed by RMI law — the jurisdiction has not enacted Local File or Master File thresholds. Defensive transfer pricing documentation is advised for intercompany PE/PP granule resale transactions exceeding USD 1,000,000 annually in order to withstand audits in counterparty jurisdictions; the functional currency and statutory currency of the RMI is the U.S. dollar.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) — the preferred benchmark for commodity-grade polyethylene and polypropylene granules
Resale Price Method — appropriate for routine distribution and logistics functions
Cost Plus Method — suited to toll-conversion or bagging/silo handling services
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) — the most practical approach for a limited-risk trading intermediary
Profit Split Method — reserved for integrated supply-chain arrangements with significant intangible value
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are not enacted in the Marshall Islands. The non-resident BC is required only to maintain a licensed registered agent, a registered office, and current corporate records in the RMI; local board meetings, local staff, and local premises are not required. However, OECD Global Forum, FATF, and foreign tax-residence standards require substantive commercial functions (negotiation, price risk, logistics control, and title passage) to be documented at the entity's true place of management, particularly where the entity is treated as tax-resident in a user jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of the Non-Resident Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting real merchandise or brokerage operations inside the Marshall Islands — such as on-island polymer storage, invoicing, or delivery — while claiming the non-resident BC exemption and omitting the 3.0% Gross Revenue Tax; this includes routing RMI-source commissions through offshore accounts to conceal taxable gross revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive assessment of 3% GRT on all concealed gross revenue, interest at the statutory rate, a negligence/evasion penalty of up to 50% of the tax due, and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act 1989 carrying a fine of up to US$1,000 and imprisonment of up to 3 years, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the BC is used as a sham: directors who authorized false GRT returns or diverted RMI-source revenue are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax; the High Court may impose asset freezes and travel bans pending prosecution, and convicted directors may be disqualified from managing RMI entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the BC as a pure shell through nominee shareholders, blank transfer instruments, or bearer-share arrangements, and failing to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner to the licensed registered agent and the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit — a pattern typical of sanctioned-party intermediaries in bulk petrochemical trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative strike-off by the Registrar, monetary penalties under the RMI AML/CFT Act and Beneficial Ownership Regulations (fines on legal persons up to US$100,000 on conviction), cancellation of the registered agent's endorsement, and refusal of Certificates of Good Standing, which halts Swift LC issuance and bank onboarding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face personal fines, disqualification orders, and criminal liability for false declarations on the Statement of Acknowledgment; the court may disregard the corporate shell and order the undisclosed principal's assets to be attached; imprisonment of up to 2 years applies to knowing concealment of beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations and Trade-Based Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the petrochemical trading platform to launder criminal proceeds or evade sanctions: over/under-invoicing PE/PP cargoes, presenting forged bills of lading or quality certificates against Swift irrevocable LCs, layering funds through a series of RMI BCs, or settling trades on behalf of OFAC-, EU-, or UN-sanctioned counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Freezing orders and asset forfeiture under the RMI Criminal Code and AML/CFT Act; fines up to US$100,000 for corporate entities and imprisonment for culpable natural persons; loss of correspondent banking access and designation as a shell-risk entity by global financial-action task forces.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authenticate false trade documents face civil restitution to the defrauded LC bank and criminal fraud penalties; money-laundering convictions carry imprisonment of up to 10 years; the High Court routinely imposes travel bans, passport surrender, and global asset-identification orders during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Operating While Administratively Dissolved / Registrar Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to contract, open accounts, or draw Swift LCs after administrative dissolution for non-payment of the annual franchise fee, or making false statements of capital, ownership, or good standing to obtain banking documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restoration of the register requires payment of all outstanding annual fees, late penalties, and reinstatement charges; contracts made in the dissolved period are voidable at the counterparty's election; outstanding fees may be doubled at the Registrar's discretion and the BC removed from the register permanently if restoration is not sought.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under BCA Section 92 and general company law, directors are personally liable for all debts contracted during the dissolved period; fraudulent declarations trigger disqualification and criminal liability; directors may be sued personally by LC banks, insurers, and cargo purchasers for losses caused by the void contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Financial Reporting / LC and Bank Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying fabricated audited financial statements, warehouse receipts, or inventory certificates to confirming banks or lenders to secure or draw under irrevocable documentary credits for polymer cargoes that do not exist or do not match the stated grade, quantity, or ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Liability under the RMI Criminal Code for forgery and fraud, U.S. wire-fraud exposure where USD clearing occurs through the Federal Reserve system, debarment from all RMI-registered agent and maritime privileges, and civil liability to confirming banks for dishonor and reimbursement; banks may report the entity to the RMI FIU and OFAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is near-automatic in documentary fraud: directors who endorse false LC documents are personally liable to the negotiating bank for amounts paid, plus interest and costs; conviction carries imprisonment; travel bans and Interpol notices may issue where cross-border cargo diversion is alleged.
